parole.testo: From the imperative of Middle High German haln (“fetch”), from Old High German holōn, from Proto-West Germanic *holōn. Comparable to modern German hallo, Spanish hola. Popularized via the telephone akin to English hello. Associated via phonetic pattern to hälsning (“greeting”), häll (“hail”).
Borrowed from Middle High German kisel, from Old High German kisil, from Proto-West Germanic *kisil, *kesul (“pebble, gravel”).
Inherited from Old Swedish libbestikka, lybbestikka, from Middle High German lübbestock, from Old High German lubistekkila, from from Proto-West Germanic *lubistik.

parole.significato: to get, to acquire, to procure
parole.testo: From Old Swedish skaffa, from Middle High German schaffen, from Old High German scaffan (from scepfen, from Proto-West Germanic *skappjan. Cognate with Old Swedish skepja (see Swedish skapa)).
